name: Coordination Structural Integrity Suite
author: Regis Lloyd Chapman
description: A suite of domain-general coordination standards in two Tensegrity families: seven compressive standards as structural floors and three generative standards, with the Precision-First Design Standard as the meta-standard. Specifications CC BY 4.0, co-released with CROSS (CC0).

baseline: Each member points at canonical source; prose is not reproduced (substrate discipline)
Version parsed from the source matches the filename and header
Candidate members carry candidate status and are excluded from conformance gating

domain.substrateDiscipline: The manifest is a descriptor that points at canonical source and carries conformance; it does not serve standard prose in place of source.

members.name: Precision-First Design Standard
members.description: The suite meta-standard. Specifies what precision requires across every standard. Precision-First Design is the discipline of keeping instruments precise enough that violations are detectable and compliance meaningful, before deployment, not after a failure has made those questions urgent. Defines two foundational principles: the precision-first invariant (precision deficit and precision imposition as two failure directions of one commitment) and Method-Structure Congruence (the epistemic method used must match the structural character of what is being known; congruence deficits are self-concealing because the absent content leaves no gap marker). Nine corollaries, the precision review checklist, and obligation loop tier requirements.

members.name: Adverse-Signal Engagement Principle Core Standard
members.description: Specifies how coordination systems engage with signals that contradict their current model. Defines what counts as an adverse signal, the three-phase processing loop, and the requirement that adverse signals not be processed as noise or threat but as structural information.
relatedStandards: Four Batteries Capacity Standard: the Relational Battery condition; a depleted Relational Battery produces a systematic false negative in the detection surface
Four Batteries Capacity Standard: Relational battery state, required to disambiguate signal-absence-under-low-trust from healthy absence
Conflict Transformation Standard: the structural conditions under which the engagement constitutes genuine transformation capacity
Structural Power Obligation Standard Section 4.4: nested and polycentric handling, subsidiarity, and concentration detection
Structural Consent Legibility Standard Section 6.4: the general principle of Cynefin action-mode calibration
Structural Power Obligation Standard Section 4.5: the seven external-override classes and their tier provisions
CRAFT Condition 1 (risk-reduction statement) and Condition 6 (feedback protocol) for cross-layer propagation of a specification-framework gap
Structural Consent Legibility Standard: the Wheel of Consent two-axis read (who acts, who benefits)

members.name: Coordination Scaling Standard
members.description: Specifies how rigor scales with coordination context. Provides the calibration framework that determines what evidence pressure is appropriate for what scale of public impact claim.

members.name: Information Asymmetry Classification Standard
members.description: Classifies the six information asymmetry classes (positional, temporal, interpretive, relational, complexity, omission) and specifies what each requires structurally.
relatedStandards: ASEP: this taxonomy is the Name-phase content; information asymmetry signals are adverse signals subject to the system's adverse-signal processing

members.name: Regenerative Obligation Standard
members.description: Specifies that extraction from contributors must be matched by regenerative return that is non-fungible, proximate, and embedded in the relationship that generated it. Obligation flows in lineage and ecological directions.
relatedStandards: Ostrom Design Principle 3: those affected by the operational rules participate in modifying them; adequacy is assigned to registered harm-bearing parties
ASEP (protection for claim-raisers) and the Four Batteries Capacity Standard (Stage D-E identity fusion as a visibility suppressor)

members.name: Structural Consent Legibility Standard
members.description: Specifies the conditions under which consent in a coordination system is structurally legible: consent is specified to particular acts and parties, standing is distributed to all parties who bear costs, and the consent act itself is verifiable rather than assumed.
relatedStandards: ASEP: the implausible absence is processed as an adverse signal through Signal Escalation
ASEP: durable, tamper-evident logging (the durable-logging requirement)
ASEP: consent failures are adverse signals subject to Signal Escalation
ASEP: adverse-signal processing
Sensemaking Standard Section 9.2 (spoken coordination channels, recording consent architecture)
IACS Extension Class C (Descriptive Capacity Asymmetry): the mechanism by which measurement vocabulary limits produce structural invisibility
ASEP: detection flags for Signal Escalation, never adjudicates
Four Batteries Capacity Standard: battery-vector stress signatures (a runtime data dependency)
IACS: the six asymmetry classes each suppress specific bandwidth types (6.3)

members.name: Structural Power Obligation Standard
members.description: Specifies that power in a coordination system must be matched by obligation directions running in multiple directions toward all cost-bearing parties. Power concentration is precisely defined as power without obligation.
relatedStandards: IACS Class 3 (Interpretive asymmetry): the information-dimension expression of interpretive capacity concentration; apply jointly in the coordination dimension at Instrumented
SCLS enduring shadow dynamic: the consent-dimension expression of exit-and-voice-ratio deterioration
Coordination Scaling Standard: the affected-party reach ceiling that triggers the channel
SCLS: what structural consent means and how it is verified; joint adoption satisfies both Authorize invariants through one consent process
SCLS Observation domain: the monitoring scope is a coordination decision subject to the Authorize invariant; an undisclosed detection surface is a consent failure
ASEP: unauthorized concentration is an adverse signal; the implausible absence of monitoring results is itself an adverse signal

members.name: Conflict Transformation Standard
members.description: Specifies that conflicts in a coordination system must be engageable at less than their full intensity before they reach termination thresholds. Requires graduated engagement architecture and the structural capacity to hold conflict as information rather than process it as a binary.

members.name: Four Batteries Capacity Standard
members.description: Specifies the four capacity dimensions that sustain coordination work: Mission battery, Contribution battery, Relational battery, and a fourth. Requires that depletion in any dimension be reportable as a structural condition rather than left as a private experience.

members.name: Sensemaking Standard
members.description: Specifies the structural conditions for sensemaking in a coordination system: disruption-occasioned, action-entangled, sufficiency-oriented, and particular-to-general. Requires that disruption events open as questions the system needs to answer rather than be processed as resolved.
relatedStandards: Four Batteries Capacity Standard: the conformant capacity framework whose Personal, Relational, Contribution, and Mission batteries map to the four capacity categories
ASEP: a signal remains subject to Signal Escalation timing regardless of whether the sensemaking process that would classify it has completed
SPOS: sensemaking-failure classification authority is a coordination-dimension power concentration subject to the Authorize invariant
IACS: sensemaking capacity asymmetry is invisible to the six-class taxonomy; Four Batteries Connection 6 (battery-state differentials) supplies the measurement surface
IACS: personal-framing misapplication (3.2) is the predictable output of Class 3 Interpretive Asymmetry, warranting both a sensemaking and an asymmetry investigation

members.name: Conflict Transformation Preconditions Specification
members.description: A supporting specification (release candidate) for the preconditions the Conflict Transformation Standard assumes.

members.name: Frame Language Foundational Vocabulary Specification
members.description: Stable foundational vocabulary specification. Adjacent to the suite, not a structural floor.
